newsitem.title: UK: Lebanon mark Eurobond seen in early June-bankers.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon mark Eurobond seen in early June-bankers.

text.p: Lebanon could make its debut in the mark Eurobond sector as soon as early June, bankers said on Wednesday.
Lebanon said last week it planned to raise 250 million marks in five-year Eurobonds. Commerzbank and Societe Generale, appointed as underwriters, declined to comment on terms of the deal.
Bankers elsewhere said Lebanon could launch the issue in early June, after investor presentations. Lebanon was expected to pay between 150 and 175 basis points over Libor on the bonds, they said.
Lebanon said the terms and conditions for the issue would be determined in the coming weeks. The country has tapped the international bond markets before, but only the dollar sector.
It issued a three-year dollar bond in 1994 and a five-year deal in 1995. The coupons on the deals were 10.125 percent and 9.125 percent respectively.
In March, Lebanon's acting finance minister Fouad Siniora said Lebanon wanted to issue mark bonds because interest rates were lower than in the dollar market.
